stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Universal Music Group is launching a new AI music platform utilizing its licensed catalog.
The platform, developed with ElevenLabs, enables users to create remixes and mashups from existing tracks.
This represents a significant industry shift in how music catalogs can be leveraged using generative AI.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes key ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It indicates the model is relevant to the text-generation pipeline within the AI/ML ecosystem.
The associated tags confirm its connection to key technologies like transformers, safetensors, and Llama.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model, a significant LLM from Meta.
It is featured on Hugging Face Benchmarks, indicating community interest and performance tracking.
The context involves standard NLP pipelines (text-generation) using popular ML libraries (transformers, safetensors).

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed to handle multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling locally.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when utilized with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Slack can now vibe-code interactive charts and reports inside chats
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Slack is integrating AI-powered 'Slackforce Surfaces' to allow users to build interactive content directly within chat.
This new feature enables the creation of reports, dashboards, polls, and microsites using natural language prompts to a Slackbot.
The AI leverages information from existing conversations and connected enterprise apps like Google Drive and Salesforce.

stories.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Big Tech companies are actively influencing K-12 education by providing AI-related curriculum and resources.
The narrative suggests that proficiency in these new technologies is becoming essential for student success and job readiness.
This trend represents a significant industry shift where tech creators are partnering with schools to drive AI adoption.

stories.title: Electric air taxis get the green light for test flights in Texas
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: A new federal program is launching in Texas to test electric, hybrid-electric, and autonomous aircraft.
The testing is beginning before the final regulatory rules for this advanced air mobility technology are established.
The FAA's eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP) has selected eight state-led initiatives for this testing.

stories.title: Panic builds over bankrupt Spirit’s looming data sale to Google
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy proceedings are linked to a potential data sale to Google.
The news raises concerns about the commodification of personal data in the context of AI development.
The article critiques the idea that corporate bankruptcy should lead to a 'land grab' for valuable data assets.

stories.title: GPU-CFR: 80x Faster Counterfactual Regret Minimization by Compiling the Game to Static Dataflow and CUDA Graph Replay
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Addresses a performance bottleneck where Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR) runs faster on CPUs than GPUs.
Introduces GPU-CFR, a method that achieves an 80x speedup by compiling the game to static dataflow and using CUDA Graph Replay.
Highlights the issue of kernel launch overhead dominating runtime in previous GPU implementations for tree-sweeping workloads.

stories.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Introduces Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM) to address gaps in traditional marketing data regarding AI-generated content.
Develops a causal inference framework to estimate the business impact of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Generative Engine Marketing (GEM).
GMMM integrates metrics like repeated generated answers, question counts, and notice probabilities to quantify marketing effectiveness in generative AI environments.

stories.title: Artificial Id: Drive and Persistent Alignment in Agentic AI
stories.author: Yakov Pyotr Shkolnikov
bullet_points: Addresses the control problem in advanced Agentic AI systems that maintain consequential state across tasks.
Proposes an 'artificial id' as an adaptive internal drive to govern when AI behavior should continue, stop, or change.
Moves beyond current methods where behavioral transitions (objectives, retries) are specified externally by humans.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a multi-signal pipeline for detecting domain-specific hallucinations in LLMs.
The pipeline integrates DeBERTa-v3 classification, MC Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark for response-level detection.

stories.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Introduces Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM) to address limitations in current marketing data regarding AI-generated content.
Develops a causal inference framework to estimate the business impact of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Generative Engine Marketing (GEM).
GMMM integrates metrics like repeated generated answers, question counts, and notice probabilities to quantify marketing effectiveness in generative AI environments.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in LLMs, addressing unfaithful claims in generated text.
The detection method combines fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark across general and specific tasks.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in LLMs, addressing the issue of unfaithful claims.
The detection method combines fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance on the HaluEval benchmark, demonstrating strong results (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on general and specific tasks.

stories.title: Rust Is Tier-1 Language at Microsoft
stories.author: rustfoundation.org via mmastrac
bullet_points: Microsoft has officially designated Rust as a Tier-1 language within its development ecosystem.
This indicates a significant strategic shift towards adopting Rust for core Microsoft technologies.
The move signals growing industry acceptance and enterprise-level validation of Rust's capabilities.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded model support.
Integration with GGUF models via llama.cpp enhances compatibility across various hardware.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Meta’s Muse AI works and creeps me out
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta has released its new AI assistant, Muse, signaling a push into AI-powered productivity tools.
Muse is designed to automate routine tasks such as online shopping, email management, and trip planning.
The article offers a hands-on review, highlighting the dual nature of the tool's functionality (helpful vs. unsettling).

stories.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: LinkedIn successfully defended against lawsuits related to scanning users' Chrome extensions.
The judge dismissed the lawsuits, finding no evidence of a genuine privacy violation by LinkedIn.
The case highlights ongoing legal scrutiny regarding how platforms monitor user activity via browser extensions.

stories.title: Europe will go it alone on Venus mission after NASA yanks radar instrument
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: Europe is independently pursuing a Venus mission following NASA's decision to withdraw a radar instrument.
The shift suggests a potential realignment of international space partnerships, with Europe potentially looking toward China.
The news highlights ongoing tensions or changes in NASA's international collaboration strategies.

stories.title: Android can now securely migrate your logins between password managers
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Android now supports secure migration of login credentials between password managers.
The feature is currently limited in terms of application support.
Google has indicated that broader app compatibility is planned for future updates.

stories.title: China’s drone supremacy shows in airlifting bodies and food after Nepal flood disaster
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: DJI drones are being utilized in Nepal for disaster relief efforts following severe flooding.
The drones, previously used for high-altitude logistics like Mount Everest supply, are now performing critical aid functions.
The incident highlights the growing practical application and deployment of commercial drone technology in humanitarian crises.

stories.title: Four groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Four distinct groups were identified using an identical exploit kit targeting Chrome and Windows.
The vulnerability exploitation is linked to a 'patch gap' in system updates.
The accelerating discovery of vulnerabilities, potentially aided by AI, is cited as a contributing factor.

stories.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
stories.author: Li Charlie Xia
bullet_points: Addresses the core ML challenge of generalization under distribution shift.
Proposes a new concept, $\gamma^*$-concept shifts, to address limitations in existing shift definitions.
Utilizes entropic optimal transport to bridge the gap between theoretical learning bounds and practical applications.

stories.title: Can Edge-Deployable Vision-Language Models Identify Species?
stories.author: Yi Ding
bullet_points: The research focuses on evaluating small, edge-deployable Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for species identification in remote camera trap applications.
The study tests VLMs in the 2B-8B parameter range (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Gemma3) against a domain specialist (BioCLIP) on a 96-species task.
The core relevance is demonstrating if smaller, practical models possess genuine taxonomic knowledge suitable for real-world, low-connectivity field deployment.

stories.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
stories.author: Manling Li
bullet_points: Introduces MindTopo, a new benchmark designed to test foundation models' ability to perform topological reasoning.
Highlights a gap in current AI evaluation, which primarily focuses on metric properties (distance, shape) rather than topological invariants.
Connects the research to cognitive science, suggesting topological relations are fundamental to human spatial understanding.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to autonomously enhance their capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines a progression toward 'recursive meta-improvement,' moving through stages of autonomy in execution, strategy, experience acquisition, and environment adaptation.

stories.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
stories.author: Li Charlie Xia
bullet_points: Addresses the core ML challenge of generalization under distribution shift.
Proposes a new concept, $\gamma^*$-concept shifts, to handle mismatches between source and target data supports.
Bridges the gap between theoretical learning bounds and practical, sample-estimable applications in ML.

stories.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
stories.author: Luke Zettlemoyer
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of data repetition on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, a dominant sparse architecture.
Addresses a gap in research concerning how data repetition affects sparse models, unlike previous studies on dense Transformers.
Examines the effects of varying data repetition rates across different MoE configurations and data mixes.

stories.title: TART: A Modular Tool for Technique-Aware Audio-to-Tablature Guitar Transcription
stories.author: Gopala Anumanchipalli
bullet_points: Introduces TART, a new modular pipeline for Audio-to-Tablature Guitar Transcription.
Addresses key limitations in current Automatic Music Transcription (AMT), specifically expressive techniques (slides, bends) and noise robustness.
The system is designed as a four-stage pipeline to improve accuracy in real-world, noisy audio environments.

stories.title: CausalArena: Benchmarking Causal Discovery in the Foundation Model Era
stories.author: Han-Jia Ye
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of benchmarking causal discovery methods, a field crucial for scientific reasoning.
It highlights inconsistencies in current evaluation practices, specifically regarding structural causal models (SCMs), graph families, and protocols.
The rise of Causal Discovery Foundation Models (CDFMs) introduces new complexities to the existing evaluation landscape.

stories.title: 3D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Rajalakshmi Nandakumar
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of Novel View Synthesis (NVS) for millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar.
The proposed method utilizes 3D Point Splatting to create a physically faithful, complex-valued, and multi-viewpoint-tractable renderer.
It overcomes limitations of prior methods, such as Differentiable Monte Carlo ray tracers, which lack scalability for multi-view optimization.

stories.title: CoRA-NAS: Coarse Ranking and Anchor-Residual Refinement for Neural Architecture Search
stories.author: Jiaojiao Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces CoRA-NAS, a two-stage framework for Neural Architecture Search (NAS).
Combines a static ranking prior (CoRA-Rank) with low-cost learning-curve refinement (CoRA-Refine).
Addresses the reliability issue of zero-cost proxies in NAS by using consensus mechanisms and anchor sampling.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to autonomously enhance their capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines a progression from basic improvement autonomy to advanced recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
stories.author: Luke Zettlemoyer
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of repeating training data on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, a dominant sparse architecture.
Addresses the practical issue of data scarcity in NLP, where training data is often reused.
Examines how data repetition affects MoE models across different repetition rates and domain mixes.

stories.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
stories.author: Manling Li
bullet_points: Introduces MindTopo, a new benchmark designed to test topological intuition in foundation models.
Highlights the gap in current AI evaluation, which heavily favors metric properties (distance, angle) over topological relations.
Aims to bridge cognitive science findings on spatial understanding with the capabilities of large language models.

stories.title: Nuha-Speech: Building General-Purpose Arabic Speech-LLMs
stories.author: Muhammad Alqurishi
bullet_points: Addresses the significant underrepresentation of Arabic in multilingual Speech Large Language Models (speech-LLMs).
Introduces Nuha-Speech, a comprehensive initiative focused on developing general-purpose Arabic speech-LLMs.
The project covers the entire pipeline, including dataset construction, model training, and systematic evaluation, specifically focusing on Arabic Speech Question-Answering (SQA).

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to persistently enhance their capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines a progression from basic execution autonomy to advanced recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: RetroThinker: Enabling Retrospective Thinking in Speech LLMs
stories.author: David Harwath
bullet_points: RetroThinker aims to improve complex reasoning in Speech LLMs by enabling retrospective thinking.
SpeechLLMs offer advantages over traditional ASR/text-LM pipelines (lower latency, nuance retention) but struggle with complex reasoning.
The research addresses the challenge of enhancing reasoning in real-time spoken interactions without violating strict latency constraints.

stories.title: Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin
stories.author: fnthawar2
bullet_points: Shopify is undergoing a significant platform technology shift.
The company is migrating away from React Native for mobile development.
The new focus is on native development using Swift (iOS) and Kotlin (Android).

stories.title: The Deathray: A simple way for an untrusted site to freeze a Mac
stories.author: auberonedu
bullet_points: A vulnerability named 'The Deathray' allows untrusted websites to freeze macOS.
The attack exploits a weakness in how macOS handles certain web interactions.
This represents a significant client-side security risk for Mac users.

stories.title: Technique for Manipulating Satellite Photos Now Reveals Ancient Images (2025)
stories.author: gumby
bullet_points: A technique originally developed for manipulating satellite photos is being repurposed.
This technique has demonstrated the ability to reveal ancient images.
The development is linked to NASA technology transfer spinoffs.

stories.title: Forgejo 16.0.4 has a critical security bug fix (RCE - Remote Code Execution)
stories.author: codeberg.org via brn
bullet_points: Forgejo, a self-hosted Git service, has released version 16.0.4.
The update addresses a critical security vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as Remote Code Execution (RCE), requiring immediate attention from users.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article posits that AI is becoming highly proficient at coding tasks.
It argues that coding itself is not the most critical skill in software development.
This suggests a shift in the value proposition for human developers towards higher-level tasks.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation is accelerating rapidly.
The primary challenge is not generation speed, but code correctness.
The article addresses the 'verification bottleneck' in AI-assisted software development.

stories.title: Beyond LLMs: How World Models Are Changing Generative Media
stories.author: blackgirlbytes
bullet_points: The article discusses the shift in generative AI from Large Language Models (LLMs) to World Models.
World Models aim to simulate and understand the underlying dynamics of the real world, moving beyond pure text generation.
The introduction uses a relatable analogy (a toddler's reaction to liquids) to illustrate the concept of predictive, embodied understanding.
